result.title: FrontierPhysics: Evaluating Agents for End-to-End Physics Research
result.comment: 41 pages (10 pages main text), 19 figures, 11 tables
result.summary: AI agents are playing an increasingly important role in physics research. However, existing physics benchmarks only evaluate fixed questions, isolated sub-tasks, or paper reproduction with given solutions, and rarely check research quality alongside correctness. We introduce FrontierPhysics, an end-to-end benchmark with 56 tasks made by 42 physicists based on their own research, covering nine domains across theoretical, computational, and experimental physics. Each task requires agents to review the literature, develop a research plan, conduct research and experiments, and produce structured outputs and scientific manuscripts. Combining deterministic verifiers with expert-authored rubrics, FrontierPhysics evaluates whether agents' research is correct and publishable. Across 22 models in 26 configurations, no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Manual review of agent trajectories shows that frontier agents' main weaknesses are insufficiently rigorous reasoning and limited expert intuition, rather than gaps in physics knowledge or execution errors.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 FrontierPhysics，一个由物理学家基于自身研究设计的 56 个端到端物理研究任务基准，要求智能体完成文献调研、制定计划、开展实验并撰写结构化输出与手稿，并用确定性验证器加专家评分表同时考察正确性与可发表性。
AI.relevance_reason: 虽不涉及视觉或 latent 状态，但其对长程轨迹中证据获取、计划推进与「正确性 vs 研究质量」双重评价的设计，可能为 LVR 的推理过程评价与停止决策提供参照，可供核查。
